description: These three NetLogo agent-based decision support pilots from the EU-funded AntifragiCity project simulate urban mobility when critical infrastructure is disrupted, as part of its Deliverable D3.4 Mobility Triage Analysis DSS. The Bratislava model represents roads, tram, bus and ferry networks across the Danube and tests closures of one to all three bridges with modal-share shifts and temporary ferries, tracking throughput, trips of vulnerable travellers, efficiency, redundancy and a Theil inequity index in the first ten minutes after a disruption. The Odessa model simulates evacuation of the city centre from bomb shelters after an attack on the port, with civilians switching into pedestrians or cars, responders collecting vulnerable people and A* pathfinding; evacuation points are assumed because city plans were not public. The Larissa model routes household and resource-seeking trips on road and bus networks under user-set flood severity over a flood-prone area mapped from historical records. Networks come from OpenStreetMap processed in QGIS, with population and income patches. They were built by Anastasia Tzioutziou and released on Zenodo on 24 June 2026 as version 1.0, each with the .nlogo file, shapefiles and an ODD protocol; Zenodo lists CC BY 4.0 while the repository LICENSE files are CC BY-NC 4.0. Caveats: results are short-horizon and depend on assumed parameters. They support agent-based emergency response and resilience planning for transport; a related record is the CHIME hurricane evacuation model.
